The title links the public scandal of 12:30 to this confession, and later uses in 12:78 and 12:88 show the title migrating in the surah while this local word frames the wife's identity.
words.root_gloss_range: strength, might, rank, and powerful authority; here the human title supplies institutional pressure rather than divine authority

words.gloss_range: definite temporal now marking the decisive disclosure point
words.prose: {{ar:الْآنَ}} ({{tr:al-āna}}) makes the confession's timing decisive. The definite now divides concealment from manifestation, so the wife does not merely state content; she marks the moment when truth arrives. Its uniqueness in this surah strengthens the sense of a singular turning point.

topics.headline: decisive now

words.gloss_range: active hapax disclosure verb picturing truth as separating out and settling
words.prose: {{ar:حَصْحَصَ}} ({{tr:ḥaṣḥaṣa}}) is a rare, reduplicated disclosure verb. In the canonical active reading, truth becomes the grammatical actor: it clarifies, separates out, and settles into visibility. The repeated consonantal texture makes that clearing audible as iterative clarification. The passive variant usefully shows another possible theological pressure, but the local received form foregrounds truth's active manifestation. Its hapax status makes the confession moment linguistically singular, with 12:100 later returning to the truth-root completion.
words.root_gloss_range: separating out, making distinct, and settled clarification; here the hapax reduplicated verb marks decisive disclosure

topics.headline: active truth manifestation

topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect verb, and the following definite truth noun functions as the active subject in the canonical reading.

topics.headline: reduplicated clarifying force

topics.headline: hapax disclosure provenance (12:51, 12:100)

words.gloss_range: definite truth/right as subject and actor of disclosure

The word gathers epistemic truth and judicial rightness together: what becomes clear is also what restores Joseph's rightful standing. Links to 12:26 and 12:100 show the surah's delayed verification arc, while divine-epithet parallels such as 6:62, 22:6, and 23:116 remain resonance rather than a local name-reading.
words.root_gloss_range: truth, reality, right, justice, and due firmness; here the definite subject makes truth/right the actor in disclosure

words.gloss_range: independent first-person pronoun foregrounding self-assigned agency
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَا}} ({{tr:anā}}) is grammatically more than the verb needs. After truth has been said to become clear, the independent first-person pronoun makes that truth personal. By placing it before the confession verb, the wife foregrounds herself as agent and narrows responsibility away from the wider group.

words.gloss_range: first-person Form III confession of sustained attempted pressure against Joseph
words.prose: {{ar:رَاوَدتُّهُ}} ({{tr:rāwadttuhu}}) is the wife's owned version of the earlier charge. The first-person marking, the preceding explicit pronoun, and the object suffix compress agent and target into one confession. Form III keeps the action as attempted pressure rather than completed success, preserving Joseph's refusal while making her agency unmistakable. The same verb-frame answers word 5 inside 12:51.
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, attempting, soliciting, and gradual pressure; here Form III narrows the range to sustained attempted solicitation

words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, person, life, and desire; here the possessed singular self is the targeted moral and personal referent

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) prevents the wife's statement from stopping at self-blame. It attaches a positive attestation about Joseph to the confession, so admission and vindication become one continuous testimony.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle plus suffix launching Joseph's vindication clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) launches the final attestation with emphasis and binds that emphasis directly to Joseph through the suffix. The vindication is therefore strengthened from its first word, not merely appended to the confession, and the emphatic claim about God's knowledge in 12:50 is answered by emphatic public attestation here.

topics.headline: emphatic vindication start
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final claim begin as emphatic vindication focused on Joseph.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle carries a third masculine suffix and opens the final predicate clause.

topics.headline: emphasis handoff from divine knowledge

topics.reason: The boundary row links prior emphasis to this emphatic particle without changing the local clause function.

words.gloss_range: second emphatic layer intensifying the truthfulness verdict
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) adds a second layer of assertion inside the final attestation. The clause builds force step by step: emphatic opening, emphatic prefix, then class-membership verdict.

topics.headline: second emphasis layer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the truthfulness claim intensify rather than remain a plain predicate.

words.gloss_range: membership preposition classifying Joseph among truthful people
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) routes the verdict into class membership. Joseph is not merely said to be correct in one incident; he is placed among the recognized truthful.

topics.headline: truthful class membership

words.gloss_range: definite plural active-participle class giving Joseph durable truthfulness
words.prose: {{ar:الصَّادِقِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ṣādiqīna}}) ends the ayah on Joseph's vindicated character. The definite plural class and active-participle form make truthfulness durable and recognized, not a one-time correct statement. The triple emphasis of the final clause makes the wife's testimony especially weighty because it comes against her own interest. Same-surah links to 12:17, 12:26, 12:46, and 12:82 show competing truth-claims resolved here in Joseph's favor, while broader parallels such as 4:87 and 4:122 remain class-resonance rather than the local source of meaning.
words.root_gloss_range: truthfulness, veracity, confirming, and moral reliability; here the active-participle plural gives Joseph durable class membership among truthful people

topics.headline: durable character verdict

topics.reason: The active participle and self-incriminating witness context support characterological truthfulness, not merely factual correctness.
